chunks: He asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of God and their derivation — from what is 'Allah' derived? He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hisham! Allah is derived from ilah (God), and ilah necessitates a worshipper. The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning has committed disbelief and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning has committed shirk and worshipped two. Whoever worships the meaning without the name — that is tawhid. Do you understand, O Hisham?'

He said: I said: Give me more. He said: 'God has ninety-nine names. If the name were the named, then each name would be a god. But God is a meaning to which these names point, and all of them are other than Him. O Hisham! Bread is a name for the edible, water is a name for the drinkable, cloth is a name for the wearable, and fire is a name for the burning. Do you understand, O Hisham — an understanding with which you can repel and contend against our enemies who take others alongside God, Mighty and Majestic?' I said: Yes.
So he said: 'May God benefit you with it and establish you, O Hisham!' He (Hisham) said: By God, no one was able to subdue me in matters of tawhid until I attained this station of mine.

key_terms.إله: Ilah — the root word meaning 'God/deity', from which 'Allah' is linguistically derived
key_terms.الاسم: The name — a linguistic designation distinct from the entity it refers to
key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — divine unity; worshipping God's actual reality, not merely a linguistic label
key_terms.الشرك: Shirk — associating partners with God; here used to describe worshipping both the name and the meaning as two distinct entities
key_terms.المسمى: The named — the actual reality or entity behind the name
key_terms.مألوه: Ma'luh — one who worships; the concept that 'ilah' (deity) necessarily entails a relationship with a worshipper

ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of the name Allah and how does it relate to tawhid according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this dialogue between Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and Hisham ibn al-Hakam — one of the foremost theological defenders of Shia doctrine — the Imam explains the critical distinction between the name (ism) and the named reality (musamma). The teaching was addressed to Hisham to equip him for theological debates with opponents who conflated the Names of God with God Himself, potentially leading to a form of polytheism. The Imam illustrates with everyday analogies: bread is a name for food, not food itself; similarly, 'Allah' is a name pointing to the divine reality, not identical to it. True tawhid consists of worshipping the divine reality (meaning) rather than the name alone or both the name and the meaning as separate things.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, that, ‘He asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Names of Allahazwj and their derivatives of Allahazwj from what Heazwj is derived. So heasws said: ‘O Hisham! ‘Allah’ is derived from ‘God’, and God requires its worshipper, and the name is other than the named. So the one who worships the Name besides the Meaning, so he has blasphemed and has not worshipped anything; and the one who worships the Name and the Meaning, so he has associated (committed Shirk) and worship two; and the one who worships the Meaning besides the Name, so that is the Tawheed. Do you understand, O Hisham?’

He (Hisham) said, ‘I said, ‘Increase for me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are ninety nine Names. So if it was such that the Name was the Named, then it would be so that every Name from these would be a God. But, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Meaning, these Names indicate upon, and all of these are other than Him<sup>azwj</sup>. O Hisham! The bread is a name of the food, and the water is a name of the drink, and the cloth is a name of the garment, and the fire is a name of the incinerator. Do you understand, O Hisham? (It is) an understanding you can repulse and fight our<sup>asws</sup> enemies with and the ones who taking others along with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty’. 
 I said, ‘Yes’.

He (Hisham) said, ‘So heasws said: ‘May Allahazwj Benefit you with it and Affirm you, O Hisham!’. Hisham said, ‘So, by Allahazwj! No one was able to subdue me regarding the Tawheed (Oneness) until I rose to this status of mine’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said that he asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), about the names of Allah and their derivations and roots. “What is the root from which the word Allah is derived?” The Imam replied, “O Hisham, the word Allah is derived from ’ilah, that is, the One Who is worshipped and the One who is worshipped is supposed to be worth worshipping. The name of Allah is different from His Own self. Whoever worships the name not the meaning has become a heathen and has, in fact, worshipped nothing. Whoever worships the name and its meaning jointly, he becomes a polytheist because of worshipping two gods. Whoever worships the meaning of the word Allah only he, in reality, has worshipped the One Allah (God). O Hisham, did you grasp it?”

Hisham requested, “Kindly enlighten me more.” The Imam added, “Allah has ninety-nine names. If each name had a separate meaning then each meaning would have been a god. Allah is One only and all His names stand for just One reality and all these names are other than Allah Himself. O Hisham, bread is the name of something to eat. Water is the name of something to drink. Dress is the name of something to wear on. Fire is the name of something that burns. O Hisham, did you fully grasp the point so you can defend your belief and contest successfully against our opponents, who, along with Allah, the Exalted, the Great, except things other than Him?” Hisham replied, “Yes, I did understand.”

The Imam said, “O Hisham, may Allah benefit you thereby and grant you steadfastness.” Hisham (the narrator) says, “I swear by Allah, no one has ever defeated me on the issue of the Oneness of Allah until now.”
